items.title: Atorvastatin protects cardiomyocytes from doxorubicin toxicity by modulating YAP/TAZ signaling.
items.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a widely used anthracycline chemotherapeutic agent; however, its clinical efficacy is hampered by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, which can lead to irreversible heart failure. Despite extensive research, effective strategies for preventing or mitigating DOX-induced cardiac injury remain lacking. The Hippo signaling effectors, Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional co-activator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ), are known to regulate cardiomyocyte survival, apoptosis, and mitochondrial quality control; however, their role in protecting the heart from DOX toxicity remains unclear. In this study, we investigated whether atorvastatin, a widely prescribed HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor with pleiotropic effects, attenuated DOX-induced cardiomyopathy by modulating the YAP/TAZ signaling axis. In H9c2 cardiomyocytes, DOX suppressed the expression of YAP and TAZ, leading to the downregulation of their downstream targets, Survivin and Park2, and activation of apoptotic cascades. Atorvastatin pretreatment restored YAP/TAZ expression at both mRNA and protein levels and reversed DOX-induced apoptosis. RNA interference-mediated knockdown of YAP or TAZ abolished the protective effects of atorvastatin, confirming the importance of this pathway. In a murine model of DOX cardiotoxicity, atorvastatin preserved left ventricular systolic function, reduced myocardial apoptosis and fibrosis, and restored YAP/TAZ, Survivin, and Park2 expression in the cardiac tissue. These findings suggest that atorvastatin exerts cardioprotective effects by restoring YAP/TAZ-mediated anti-apoptotic and mitochondrial quality control signaling. Our study highlights a novel mechanism via which atorvastatin mitigates DOX-induced cardiotoxicity and supports the therapeutic potential of YAP/TAZ modulation for cardioprotection.

items.title: Outcomes of rescue procedures in patients undergoing unsuccessful deployment of transcatheter mitral valve replacement.
items.abstract: Perivalvular leak (PVL), valve embolization, and migration of valve in mitral position are critical complications of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). To date, rescue strategies, and outcomes following unsuccessful initial TMVR deployment remain poorly documented. Between March 2016 and December 2024, 86 patients with high risk of open-heart surgery underwent TMVR with a balloon expandable valve at a single institution. 19.8% (17/86) of patients experienced unsuccessful first TMVR (unsuccessful group) due to valve embolization, migration, significant PVL, or pericardial effusion, whereas 80.2% (69/86) had successful first TMVR (successful group). We evaluated postoperative outcomes comparing unsuccessful to successful groups. Among 17 patients with unsuccessful first TMVR, 70.6% (12/17) underwent additional valve deployment, with successful valve-in-valve implantation in 75.0% (9/12). 17.6% (3/17) developed valve embolization in left atrium after transcatheter rescue procedures or additional valve deployment failed, subsequently 66.7% (2/3) required emergent surgical explantation of embolized valves, 33.3% (1/3) was managed medically due to prohibitive surgical risk. Surgical patients were discharged home without complications. Early mortality in unsuccessful group was 29.4% (5/17) and 13.0% (9/69) in successful group. There was no significant difference in early mortality between the 2 groups (p = 0.10). Median follow-up term was 10 months. Cumulative survival rate in 12 months was 50.5% in unsuccessful group, and 60.0% in successful group. Mid-term outcomes were similar between the 2 groups (p = 0.34). The study was underpowered to detect differences in all-cause mortality, but unsuccessful deployment was associated with substantially higher numerical early mortality and significantly higher cardiac mortality.

items.title: Exercise for Older People with Heart Failure and Frailty: Should We Even Try?
items.abstract: The benefits of exercise in older patients with heart failure (HF) and frailty are twofold: (i) improvement in cardiopulmonary capacity, thus reducing HF-related sequelae; (ii) attenuation of decline in physical function, thus improving frailty status. Despite the clear benefits, exercise training (ET) remains underutilised as a treatment modality in this patient population. Guidelines on the specific type of exercise intervention best suited for this population are still lacking. In this review, we discuss (i) pathophysiology underlying exercise intolerance in patients with HF; (ii) impact of frailty on HF and exercise capacity; (iii) benefits and safety of ET; (iv) recommended ET programme for this population; (v) mode of delivery and (vi) potential barriers in the uptake of ET and strategies to overcome them. An effective ET intervention in this population warrants individualisation to patient's physical capacity, while addressing possible barriers to uptake so as to ensure sustained participation in the programme.

items.title: Association of serum uric acid during pre-pregnancy with adverse pregnancy outcomes among women conceived by in-vitro fertilization: a retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Maternal serum uric acid (UA) levels have been linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes, but no studies have yet examined this association in women undergoing assisted reproductive technology. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between pre-pregnancy UA levels and adverse pregnancy outcomes in women conceived via in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET). This retrospective cohort study included 2 111 singleton pregnancies conceived via IVF-ET, delivered at Peking University Third Hospital between 1 January 2017 and 30 April 2022. Restricted cubic splines were used to test nonlinear relationships between serum UA during pre-pregnancy and adverse outcomes, and multivariable logistic regression to calculate odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval (CI). Of the 2 111 women, no significant associations were found between pre-pregnancy UA levels and preeclampsia, preterm birth, or macrosomia. However, a J-shaped relationship was observed for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and low birth weight (LBW), and an inverse U-shaped relationship for gestational hypertension (GH). Reflecting these distinct non-linear topologies, statistically significant peak risks were observed and reported at different strata: women in the higher quintile (4th quintile) of UA had a 3.20-fold increased risk of GH (adjusted OR 3.20, 95% CI 1.23, 8.33) and a 1.38-fold increased risk of GDM (adjusted OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.01, 1.88) compared with the lowest quintile. Conversely, the risk of LBW accelerated sharply and peaked at the highest quintile (5th quintile) (adjusted OR 1.98, 95% CI 1.11, 3.54). In the subgroup analysis, the positive association between pre-pregnancy UA and LBW was more pronounced among patients with day 5 embryo transfer. These findings suggest that optimizing serum UA levels in women planning pregnancy, particularly those undergoing IVF-ET, may have important clinical implications for improving pregnancy outcomes.

items.title: GlycA-gene interactions in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: evidence from genetic association.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular-Kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a concept introduced by the American Heart Association, describing systemic diseases resulting from the pathophysiological interaction among obesity, stroke, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Glycoprotein acetyls (GlycA) is a novel biomarker for systemic inflammation and cardiovascular risk. This study aims to uncover the shared genetic architecture between GlycA and CKM, identify common risk loci and key tissues, and clarify the mechanisms linking these conditions. Using summary data from large-scale GWAS studies, we evaluated both global and local genetic correlations between GlycA and various components of CKM. A cross-trait pleiotropic analysis was conducted to identify shared pleiotropic loci and related genes. FUSION was used to find susceptibility genes linked to GlycA and CKM. A comprehensive set of functional annotations and tissue-specific analyses was performed to uncover potential connections between these traits. Furthermore, a multi-trait colocalization method was utilized to explore the underlying mechanisms of the association between GlycA and CKM. Our study revealed a close genetic correlation between GlycA and CKM. We identified 260 potential SNPs that were corrected using the Bonferroni method, of which 30 passed the colocalization test (PP.H4 > 0.70). Notably, locus 9q34.2 appeared in both GlycA-T2D and GlycA-HF trait pairs. By integrating post-GWAS methods, we identified 53 potentially drug targets (CMIP, DNAJC5G, FCGRT, etc.). FUSION analysis identified 23 shared susceptibility genes for GlycA and CKM (ZPR1, IL6R, PABPC4, etc.). Analysis of tissue enrichment at the SNP level revealed pleiotropic mechanisms associated with whole blood and liver. Gene-level analysis highlighted important roles of metabolic signaling pathways. Furthermore, multi-trait colocalization analysis suggested that rs1260326 and rs2925979 may play significant roles in the mechanistic link between GlycA and CKM. Our study confirmed a significant genetic association and shared genetic structure between GlycA and CKM, revealing potential mechanisms that may be involved.

items.title: Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092).
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding risk. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal pressure and may improve outcomes, but its role in patients receiving immunoncology-based systemic therapy remains unclear. NISTIPS TRITICC-4 is a prospective, multicentre, non-interventional cohort study conducted at up to 25 centers in Germany. A total of 350 adult patients with cirrhosis and unresectable or metastatic HCC receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab will be enrolled. Patients are allocated to two cohorts: TIPS in situ plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab alone, according to routine clinical practice.The primary endpoint is time to deterioration of liver function (TTDL), defined as persistent worsening of liver parameters for >4 weeks. Secondary endpoints include overall survival, time on treatment, overall response rate, time to new extrahepatic lesions or death, and safety with focus on bleeding and TIPS-related complications.Time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models. Propensity score matching will be applied to adjust for confounding. Analyses are exploratory. This study will provide real-world evidence on the impact of TIPS in HCC patients receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and may support more individualized management strategies in this high-risk population. www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT07365930. Hepatocellular carcinoma is the most common form of primary liver cancer and often develops in people with liver cirrhosis. In many patients, the cancer cannot be treated with surgery or local procedures and systemic drug treatment is required. A commonly used first-line treatment combines atezolizumab and bevacizumab. However, patients with cirrhosis may also suffer from increased pressure in the portal vein, which can lead to complications such as bleeding from enlarged veins in the esophagus or stomach, fluid accumulation in the abdomen, and worsening liver function. Bevacizumab can increase the risk of bleeding, which may make treatment more difficult in some patients.A transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is a procedure that reduces pressure in the portal vein by creating a new connection between blood vessels inside the liver. The NISTIPS TRITICC-4 study investigates whether patients with liver cancer who have a TIPS and receive atezolizumab plus bevacizumab have different clinical outcomes compared with patients receiving the same drug treatment without TIPS.The study will include 350 patients at up to 25 centers in Germany. It will assess changes in liver function, survival, duration of treatment, tumor response, bleeding events, treatment-related complications, and quality of life. The study aims to provide real-world evidence on the potential benefits and risks of TIPS in patients with liver cancer receiving modern systemic treatment.

items.title: Calreticulin and myeloproliferative neoplasms: linking biology to targeted therapies.
items.abstract: Calreticulin (CALR) plays important roles in protein homeostasis, immune responses, and cell signaling. Mutations in the CALR gene drive BCR:ABL1-negative classical myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) through constitutive activation of the thrombopoietin receptor and generate a tumor-specific neoepitopes, providing a rationale for selective immunotherapy. This review summarizes the biological functions of wild-type calreticulin and the molecular consequences of mutant calreticulin, including loss of endoplasmic reticulum retention, altered subcellular localization, receptor activation, and immunogenic properties. It examines preclinical and clinical evidence for therapeutic strategies targeting mutant calreticulin, including peptide-based vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, T-cell engagers, and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies. Particular attention is given to INCA033989, a mutant calreticulin-targeting monoclonal antibody currently undergoing clinical evaluation, and emerging evidence of its potential to reduce the mutant cell population while preserving normal hematopoiesis. Mutant calreticulin represents a promising target for clone-directed therapy, potentially shifting MPN treatment from symptom control toward disease modification. However, the durability and clinical significance of molecular responses remain uncertain. Immune evasion, differences between mutation subtypes, and the need to demonstrate long-term clinical benefit remain important challenges. Combining calreticulin-targeted therapies with approaches addressing oncogenic signaling and inflammation may improve treatment durability and help prevent disease progression.

items.title: Abscopal effect-induced acephalic spermatozoa and testicular dysfunction implicate Cep112 and PI3K/Akt-mTOR signaling.
items.abstract: The abscopal effect, a systemic phenomenon induced by localized irradiation and associated with inflammatory factor activation, has attracted significant interest in the context of radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy. While recognized as potentially beneficial in oncology, this effect can have detrimental off-target consequences. The underlying mechanisms for abscopal effect-induced testicular dysfunction remain unclear. In this study, we observed a pronounced testicular disruption phenotype characterized by abnormalities in meiosis, blood-testis barrier integrity, and spermatid orientation. Notably, we report the novel finding that the abscopal effect can induce acephalic spermatozoa (headless sperm). Transcriptional analysis by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction revealed the dysregulation of the expression of centrosomal proteins, known regulators of meiosis and spermiogenesis. By employing RNA interference to knock down centrosomal protein 112 (Cep112), we demonstrated its critical role in spermiogenesis and established its close association with the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) and mechanistic target of rapamycin/ribosomal protein S6 (mTOR/rpS6) signaling pathways. Our findings indicate that Cep112 mediates cytoskeletal organization in testes and sperm formation via the PI3K/Akt and mTOR/rpS6 pathways, suggesting that Cep112 significantly contributes to abscopal effect-induced spermatogenic dysfunction.

items.title: Nanoengineered STING agonists for cancer therapy: toward immunodynamic control.
items.abstract: Activation of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is a mechanistically compelling strategy for cancer immunotherapy, but first-generation STING agonists have shown limited clinical activity despite clear pharmacodynamic induction of interferon-related signals. This translational gap suggests that therapeutic benefit depends not only on pathway engagement but also on where, in which cells, at what amplitude, and for how long STING is activated. In this review, we summarize the cellular context of cGAS-STING signaling, the pharmacological evolution and clinical experience of STING agonists, and the major barriers imposed by route, species differences, biological heterogeneity, and systemic inflammatory toxicity. We then examine how nanoengineering may improve agonist protection, cytosolic access, tissue and cell-type selectivity, and temporal exposure. Importantly, we distinguish improved delivery or tumor accumulation from direct evidence of altered signaling kinetics or a wider therapeutic window. Representative lipid, polymeric, inorganic, biogenic, biomimetic, antibody-directed, and prodrug-based platforms are evaluated together with mechanism-based combination sequencing, hematologic malignancy-specific considerations, biomarker-guided patient selection, repeated-dose safety, and manufacturability. Overall, nano-STING therapy should be developed toward immunodynamic control rather than simple delivery enhancement, with benefit judged by the relationship among delivery, cell-resolved pharmacodynamics, antitumor efficacy, and toxicity.

items.title: ABCD-Trial: study protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in patients with Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis for the evaluation of efficacy and safety of B-Cell Depletion with rituximab (ABCD).
items.abstract: The exact disease-causing mechanisms in ALS remain incompletely understood. A possible cause is inflammation of neurons. Compared to other neurodegenerative diseases, neuroinflammation is pronounced in ALS, presumably leading to disease progression and neuronal death. Patients with ALS can have neuronal autoantibodies and most notably antibody-producing cells in the cerebrospinal fluid. The CD20-binding therapeutic antibody rituximab targets these antibody-producing B-cells. Rituximab is a medication commonly used in neurology. Single patients with ALS have already been treated with rituximab, which was well tolerated. We therefore want to evaluate safety and efficacy of a treatment with rituximab in ALS patients in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial. With this trial we aim for slower disease progression and unveiling disease-causing mechanisms in ALS. A total of 52 male and female patients older than 18 years with active sporadic ALS and disease duration of less than 24 months who are on a stable dose of riluzole (50 mg BID) should be included. Patients requiring assisted ventilation of any kind or have a known intolerance to the study medication rituximab are excluded. The study medication rituximab or placebo should be administered over a period of 52 weeks at 4 distinct time points, followed by a follow-up period of 79 weeks with 4 visits. Treatment efficacy should be evaluated using the ALS functioning scale ALSFRS-R-SE at every study visit (except safety visits). Safety will be assessed through regular laboratory analyses, adverse event (AE) and serious adverse event (SAE) monitoring, and CD20+ B-cell kinetics. The primary endpoint is the change in the ALS Functional Rating Scale-Revised (ALSFRS-R-SE) from baseline to week 79. Trial sites will be at Charité/DZNE Berlin and DZNE Bonn. ALS is a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disease with limited treatment options. Recent preclinical in vivo studies suggest that B-cell-mediated autoimmunity contributes to disease progression. This trial will evaluate whether rituximab, which specifically depletes CD20+ B-cells, can slow ALS progression and provide insights into disease mechanisms. The trial was registered in the German WHO-recognized primary register Deutsches Register Klinische Studien DRKS (German Clinical Trials Register) on 3/07/2023 under registration number DRKS00030948.

items.title: Passive acquisition of hepatitis B virus antibodies after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.
items.abstract: Newly positive hepatitis B virus (HBV) serologic results after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) may reflect passive antibody transfer from blood-derived products rather than HBV infection. We investigated the incidence and temporal patterns of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and antibody to hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) acquisition after allogeneic HCT. We retrospectively evaluated 193 adults who underwent allogeneic HCT for hematologic diseases between May 2012 and March 2025 at a single institution in Japan. Anti-HBs, anti-HBc, and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were assessed before and after HCT. Among 180 patients who were anti-HBc negative before HCT, 6 (3.3%) developed anti-HBc positivity after HCT. Among 164 patients who were anti-HBs negative before HCT, 49 (29.9%) developed anti-HBs positivity. All patients with newly detectable antibodies remained HBsAg negative, and available HBV DNA measurements showed no evidence of active HBV infection. Among patients with subsequent follow-up measurements, anti-HBc disappeared in 3 of 3 evaluable patients after a median of 240 days, whereas anti-HBs declined or disappeared in 30 of 32 evaluable patients after a median of 119 days. Among patients receiving neither fresh frozen plasma nor intravenous immunoglobulin, anti-HBs concentrations increased significantly after HCT (p< .0001), with a greater increase among those receiving ≥24 versus ≤23 platelet transfusions (p = .0437). Newly detectable HBV antibodies were common after HCT without virologic evidence of infection, suggesting passive antibody transfer from cellular blood components, particularly platelets.

items.title: Prevalence of Y93H resistance-associated substitution in treatment-naïve hepatitis C virus genotype 1b patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1b infection remains a leading cause of chronic liver disease despite advances in direct-acting antivirals (DAAs). Resistance-associated substitutions (RASs) in the non-structural 5 A (NS5A) region, particularly the Y93H mutation, have been associated with reduced antiviral susceptibility and variable treatment outcomes. The global baseline prevalence of this substitution in treatment-naïve populations has not been systematically characterized. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered with PROSPERO. Observational and randomized studies reporting baseline NS5A Y93H prevalence in treatment-naïve HCV genotype 1b patients were identified through PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science. Data were synthesized using a random-effects model, and heterogeneity was quantified by the I² statistic. Sensitivity and publication bias analyses were performed using leave-one-out and DOI plot methods. Nine studies comprising 1,560 treatment-naïve patients from Asia and Europe, were included. The pooled prevalence of Y93H was 12% (95% CI, 6%-20%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 82.4%). Sensitivity analyses confirmed result stability, and minor asymmetry in the DOI plot suggested low publication bias. The Y93H substitution is a frequent naturally occurring variant in untreated HCV genotype 1b infection. Despite reduced clinical relevance with pangenotypic DAAs, its persistence warrants continued monitoring. Standardized sequencing and global resistance surveillance remain essential for optimizing treatment strategies and informing antiviral policy. Not applicable.

items.title: TyG index and TyG-WHtR as predictors of all-cause mortality in patients with prior hepatitis A or B virus infections.
items.abstract: This study aims to investigate the association between the triglyceride glucose (TyG) index and the TyG-to-waist-height ratio (TyG-WHtR) with the risk of all-cause mortality in patients with prior hepatitis A virus (HAV) or hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. This study was a retrospective cohort study that included patients from 1999 to 2018 with available data on HAV/HBV, TyG-related indices, and survival and mortality information. Multiple imputation methods were utilized to address missing variables. A weighted multivariable Cox regression model was employed to analyze the relationship between TyG and TyG-WHtR with all-cause mortality in the study patients. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on age, gender, smoking, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and hypertension. All analysis results were presented as hazards with a 95% confidence interval (CI). The study included a total of 6,413 patients, of which 1,692 were dead. The follow-up period concluded in December 2019, with a total duration of 119.31 ± 1.53 months. Analysis revealed that in patients with prior HAV or HBV infection, the TyG (HR: 1.22, 95%CI: 1.10-1.36) and TyG-WHtR (HR: 1.53, 95%CI: 1.34-1.75) were associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality. Separate studies conducted in patients with prior HAV or HBV infection also demonstrated an association between the TyG and TyG-WHtR indices with all-cause mortality (former: HR: 1.20, 95%CI: 1.07-1.34; latter: HR: 2.02, 95%CI: 1.49-2.74). Subgroup analysis results indicated that the association between TyG-WHtR and all-cause mortality was similar across age, gender, smoking, and hypertension groups (all P < 0.05). In patients with prior HAV or HBV infection, the TyG and TyG-WHtR indices were associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality. This study underscores the importance of the TyG and TyG-WHtR for patients with prior viral hepatitis, potentially aiding in the improvement of health management for this group. Our research is not a clinical trial. not applicable.

items.title: Early hemodynamic changes after the use of push-dose noradrenaline in patients presenting to the emergency department with septic shock: a descriptive study.
items.abstract: Although continuous noradrenaline infusion (CNI) is standard vasopressor therapy during the initial resuscitation of patients with septic shock, hemodynamic stabilization may not be immediate. Push-dose noradrenaline (PDNA) has been proposed as a temporary measure while CNI is being established. However, its clinical use, dosing, early hemodynamic response, and short-term safety in the emergency department (ED) are not well described. To address this gap, we conducted a single-center retrospective descriptive study at a tertiary care hospital in Japan in 2019. Adults with Sepsis-3 septic shock who received PDNA in the ED and were admitted to the intensive care unit were included. We assessed the context and dosing of PDNA administration, CNI use, mean arterial pressure (MAP) within 15 min after PDNA administration, and adverse events. Of 91 patients with septic shock, 50 (55%) received PDNA. PDNA was administered at CNI initiation in 25 patients, during CNI dose escalation in 6, and as rescue administration before CNI initiation in 19. The median (interquartile range [IQR]) initial PDNA dose was 20 (20-30) µg. During the 15-minute observation window, 32 (64%) patients received one bolus, 14 (28%) received two, 3 (6%) received three, and 1 (2%) received four. The directly observed median (IQR) MAP was 52 (44-61) mmHg at initial PDNA administration (n = 30) and 62 (50-68) mmHg 1 min later (n = 25). One of 36 patients evaluable for prespecified physiological adverse events experienced an adverse event; however, no serious adverse events were documented. In this single-center retrospective descriptive study, PDNA was most commonly administered at CNI initiation, and administration was followed by an early increase in median MAP. However, the noncomparative design and concurrent resuscitative interventions preclude attribution of this change solely to PDNA administration. No serious adverse events were documented; however, safety assessment was limited owing to missing data and retrospective ascertainment. These findings do not establish the effectiveness or safety of PDNA. Prospective comparative studies with standardized monitoring are required.

items.title: Value-based price corridor for bepirovirsen in chronic hepatitis B: an early health technology assessment in a cost-compressed setting.
items.abstract: We conducted an early health technology assessment (eHTA) of bepirovirsen, an investigational finite-course therapy for chronic hepatitis B. In China, low-cost generic nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) create a demanding comparator environment. The value-based price of a potential functional-cure strategy therefore depends on local comparator prices, threshold selection, cure durability, safety, monitoring requirements, and cured-state utility assumptions. A lifetime Markov model simulated bepirovirsen 300 mg/week for 24 weeks plus background NAs against comparator-specific standard-of-care options. Chinese cost inputs were valued in 2024 renminbi (RMB) and converted to US dollars using the 2024 annual average exchange rate of 7.1957 RMB per US dollar. The base case used a China-context cost-effectiveness threshold (CET) of $13,500 per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY), approximating China's 2024 gross domestic product (GDP) per capita after currency conversion, and compared it with higher threshold scenarios. Because reliable long-term relapse rates were unavailable, a 48-week maintained-response scenario set bepirovirsen efficacy to 9.0%, corresponding to the B-Clear primary-outcome rate among participants receiving background NA therapy. Bepirovirsen yielded 0.41-0.82 incremental QALYs across standard-of-care comparators. Compared with entecavir (ETV), the base case generated 0.82 additional QALYs, incurred an incremental total cost of $10,833.72 per patient at the value-based price, and avoided 906 hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases per 10,000 patients. Under the $13,500/QALY threshold, the value-based price per dose ranged from $92.92 to $367.44 across comparators. In the 48-week maintained-response scenario, the value-based price per dose was $70.29 versus ETV and ranged from $28.62 to $294.24 across comparators. The societal-perspective scenario increased the value-based price per dose to $426.41. Model-cohort expected value of perfect information (EVPI) was $0.46 million at the base-case threshold. Bepirovirsen's value-based price is conditional on comparator prices, CET selection, durability of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance, safety, monitoring needs, and cured-state utility assumptions. These eHTA results are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted within the limits of phase II-derived efficacy inputs, uncertain relapse pathways, and adverse-event and monitoring costs that cannot yet be estimated reliably.

items.title: NEK2 Promotes OSCC Invasion and Metastasis by Activating TNF-α Signaling Through Impairment of Desmosomal Adhesion.
items.abstract: NIMA-related kinase 2 (NEK2) is a cell cycle regulator aberrantly overexpressed in multiple cancers, yet its non-mitotic roles in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) invasion and metastasis remain unclear. Here, we analyzed public transcriptomic and single-cell datasets and found that NEK2 is significantly upregulated in OSCC tissues, with higher expression in cases exhibiting lymph node metastasis and associations with poor prognosis. Functional assays demonstrated that NEK2 promotes OSCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Transcriptomic and pathway analyses revealed that NEK2 activates TNF-α inflammatory signaling, and rescue experiments confirmed that the pro-invasive effects of NEK2 are largely dependent on TNF-α pathway activation. Through immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, we identified three core desmosomal proteins-desmoplakin (DSP), desmoglein-1 (DSG1), and junction plakoglobin (JUP)-as novel NEK2-interacting partners. NEK2 binding impaired desmosomal adhesion function at cell-cell junctions, and DSP overexpression partially rescued NEK2-induced TNF-α secretion, EMT, and invasion. In vivo, NEK2 knockdown suppressed xenograft tumor growth, preserved junctional desmosomal protein localization, and downregulated TNF-α target genes. Collectively, our findings uncover a NEK2-desmosome-TNF-α signaling axis that drives OSCC invasion and metastasis, providing new mechanistic insights and highlighting NEK2 as a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Total and beverage-specific alcohol use at mid-life and all-cause and cause-specific mortality: a prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: While detrimental health impacts of excessive alcohol use are well-established, potential effects of low-to-moderate drinking remain controversial. We examined the associations between total and beverage-specific alcohol intake and mortality, including cardiovascular disease (CVD), cancer (e.g., 20 site-specific cancers), and other mortality. We included 340,924 participants from UK Biobank (2006-2022). Alcohol use was categorized as: never or occasional alcohol consumption (≤ 20 g/week), low consumption (> 20 g/week to ≤ 20 g/d for men, > 20 g/week to ≤ 10 g/d for women), moderate consumption (> 20 to ≤ 40 g/d for men, > 10 to ≤ 20 g/d for women), and high consumption (> 40 g/d for men and > 20 g/d for women). We used Cox proportional hazard models to examine the associations of alcohol intake and mortality. During a mean follow-up of 13.4 years, we documented 22,381 deaths. Compared with never or occasional alcohol intake, high total alcohol intake was associated with higher mortality from all-causes (HR and 95%CI: 1.24 (1.17, 1.31)), CVD (1.14 (1.01, 1.28)), cancer (1.36 (1.26, 1.47)), and other causes (1.12 (1.02, 1.22)), whereas moderate alcohol use was associated with higher cancer mortality (1.11 (1.03, 1.20)) only. Alcohol consumption from spirits and beer/cider, even at low to moderate levels, was associated with higher mortality from all-causes, CVD, cancer, and other diseases (HRs ranging from 1.07 to 1.83). Yet, low and moderate alcohol intake from wine was associated with lower all-cause, CVD, cancer, or other mortality. Importantly, moderate to high intake of total alcohol and alcohol from beer/cider and spirits, and high wine use were particularly associated with higher mortality from multiple site-specific cancers, including mortality from head/neck, respiratory system, gastrointestinal, liver/gallbladder, hematological, female breast, and female/male genital cancers. The results suggested that low to moderate alcohol intake from spirits and beer/cider was associated with higher all-cause, CVD, cancer, and other mortality, whereas low to moderate alcohol use from wine was associated with lower all-cause, CVD, cancer, and other mortality. However, high alcohol use, regardless of beverage-type, mortality from various site-specific cancers was elevated.

items.title: Ileorectal fistula after resection of perforated sigmoid tumor and Hartmann's procedure with uterine invasion: a case report.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal fistulas are rare but serious postoperative complications, particularly when arising between the ileum and rectum. They are typically associated with complex intra-abdominal surgeries, malignancies, or inflammatory conditions. This case report presents a rare instance of ileorectal fistula formation following resection of a perforated sigmoid tumor with uterine invasion and subsequent Hartmann's procedure. A 40-year-old Kurdish woman with a history of diabetes mellitus presented with abdominal pain, weight loss, and diarrhea. Imaging revealed a large pelvic mass suggestive of a perforated sigmoid tumor invading the uterus. Emergency laparotomy confirmed the diagnosis, and Hartmann's procedure was performed. Postoperative recovery included chemotherapy. Months later, the patient returned with defecation per anus despite a colostomy, suggesting a fistula. Imaging confirmed an ileorectal fistula. During reoperation, the recurrent tumor and fistulous tract between the ileum and Hartmann's pouch were excised. Surgical repair included small bowel resection with anastomosis and ureteral reimplantation due to adjacent involvement. This case underscores the complexity of managing advanced colorectal malignancies with pelvic involvement. Ileorectal fistula is a rare but critical complication of Hartmann's procedure, necessitating individualized surgical planning and vigilant postoperative follow-up to optimize outcomes.

items.title: Optimization of 68 Ga-lactosylated human serum albumin (LSA) for PET-based quantitative evaluation of hepatic functional reserve in liver fibrosis models.
items.abstract: Accurate preoperative assessment of hepatic functional reserve (HFR) and future remnant liver function is essential for reducing postoperative morbidity and mortality after liver surgery, yet current clinical methods remain indirect and provide limited spatial and quantitative information. Here, we developed an asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)-targeted tracer for positron emission tomography (PET), [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-lactosylated human serum albumin ([ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-LSA), and systematically optimized the degree of lactosylation for hepatic imaging. Comparative evaluation of lactosylated human serum albumin constructs bearing 7 or 12 lactose moieties [LSA (7) and LSA (12)] identified LSA (12) as the preferred construct with more favorable hepatocyte targeting in vivo. [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-LSA was radiolabeled with high efficiency within 10 min at room temperature and showed favorable radiochemical stability in phosphate-buffered saline and serum. The optimized precursor was further formulated as a lyophilized kit, enabling rapid one-step 68 Ga labeling, reproducible preparation, and storage stability. In thioacetamide-induced rat liver fibrosis models, including untreated, spontaneous recovery, and pirfenidone-treated groups, [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-LSA PET/CT enabled single-time-point quantitative assessment of hepatic function, with 60 min post-injection selected as the optimal imaging time point. Hepatic uptake and liver-to-heart ratios were markedly reduced in fibrotic livers and progressively restored in recovery and treatment models. PET-derived parameters correlated with histological fibrosis, ASGPR expression, fibrogenic and apoptotic markers, and serum liver injury biomarkers. In contrast, 99m Tc-mebrofenin required serial imaging to evaluate hepatobiliary kinetics, highlighting mechanistic and workflow differences between transport-based scintigraphy and receptor-associated PET uptake imaging. Reduced hepatic uptake was also reproduced in a fibrotic mouse model. In addition, single-dose toxicity testing showed favorable acute tolerability of non-radioactive NOTA-LSA. Together, these findings support the feasibility of [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-LSA as a reproducible and quantitative PET platform for HFR imaging with translational potential.
